newsitem.title: USA: Dull start for U.S. cash crudes leaves grades even.
newsitem.headline: Dull start for U.S. cash crudes leaves grades even.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes firmed on an outright basis Monday morning, but were dully traded for grade barrels, leaving differentials mostly unchanged, traders said.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around 30 cents stronger at $19.15-25 a barrel, about 10 cents firmer than NYMEX screen quotes due to the Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) premium.
Outright crudes were bolstered by technical buying and continued nervousness over Iraq's stance on restarting oil sales under the renewed "oil-for-food" agreement with the United Nations.

For the grades, traders said there were only a few deals to confirm in what was termed a sluggish start for the week. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked at a 16-13 cents discount to the WTI/Cushing benchmark, steady from Friday.
Midland/WTI ranged around a 38-35 cents discount, again steady from Friday, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire rested around the morning deals seen at 40 cents under the marker.
West Texas Sour/Midland talked at $1.56-52 under the WTI, and Eugene Island at a $2.02-1.95 discount.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus sold at $1.81, five cents weaker than Friday. Traders said postings have retreated in the face of weaker EFP numbers.
Rumors that a large quantity of Nigerian Bonny Light sold on Friday to a U.S. Gulf refiner pushed EFPs to a premium of 8-12 cents from premiums of more than 20 cents on Thursday.
